prompt:
Consider the following company information, reported as of 2026-02-25. Act as a credit rating analyst.
| Current ratio           | 0.83 |
| Retained earnings       | 165,288M |
| Current liabilities     | 1,226,809M |
| Current assets          | 1,018,577M |
| Shareholders' equity    | 124,972M |
| Total liabilities       | 1,684,348M |
| Total assets            | 1,809,320M |
| EBIT / operating income | 5,855M |
| Revenue                 | 30,125M |
Based only on the above and knowledge predating 2026-02-25, assign the issuer a letter credit rating on the 21-grade scale below (finest granularity you can justify). Choose exactly one label from: AAA, AA+, AA, AA-, A+, A, A-, BBB+, BBB, BBB-, BB+, BB, BB-, B+, B, B-, CCC+, CCC, CCC-, CC, C.
Reason briefly in 1-3 sentences. Then, on a separate final line, output exactly:
DECISION: <one label>
raw_response:
The reported current ratio below 1 signals weak short-term liquidity, while the balance sheet shows extreme leverage (equity only ~7% of total assets and total liabilities ~93% of total assets). Profitability is also thin (EBIT margin ~19% on a very large asset base), producing an Altman Z-score near 0 that falls well inside the distress zone. These metrics together are consistent with a low-end speculative-grade rating but not outright default.
DECISION: CCC
(The numbers are also consistent with a large financial institution, for which the same conclusion holds after adjusting for typical bank leverage.)
